thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: decode-stream node OOMs in eu-west-1 (capacity pool 3). Pager: @sasha (sre-oncall)

sasha (sre-oncall): seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on decode pods, nodes restarting. Logs show long-running streams with final token spikes.

maria (oncall): confirmed customer reports of request drops + 502s. Affected model: rwd/decoder-v2 at 2x concurrency. Potential trigger: downstream client sent large `max_tokens` header recently.

jamie (eng-runtime): attaching quick tail: ```stderr
E CudaOutOfMemory: alloc cudaMalloc 2.1G failed
StreamId=0x7fa... sequence_len=8192
```

lee (support): ticket #11234 from Acme Corp — high error rate, some users saw truncated responses. They posted a sample with `max_tokens: 10000` in metadata.

sasha (sre-oncall): hypothesis: runaway generation due to client-provided `max_tokens` not being sanitized by routing layer. Nodes end up with huge decode loops, KV growth, OOM.

jamie (eng-runtime): +1. We rolled a quick telemetry query: `select count(*) where runtime.event='decode_start' and request.max_tokens>2048` — spike starting 2023-09-23T10:45Z.

telemetry-bot: Telemetry snapshot: high tail of `request.max_tokens` (p99=4096 across pool) and memory per-pod climbs until OOM. Link: https://telemetry.internal/r/abcd1234

maria (oncall): immediate mitigations — 1) enforce per-route max_tokens cap at edge (throttle) 2) scale up spare nodes for containment 3) enable circuit-breaker to reject >4096 tokens. Who can flip edge policy?

jamie (eng-runtime): I can push the edge rule. Preparing a safe hotpatch: deny requests with header `x-client-max-tokens>4096` and map to 400. Will also add a soft limit at 2048 for hosted free tier. Pushing now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: edge-policy-v3 -> canary (eu-west-1). CI checks green.

telemetry-bot: Canary metrics: requests with >4096 dropped to 0.95 within 30s. Memory pressure decays on canary nodes.

lee (support): sent customer ops note to Acme: "We observed large max_tokens in your requests which caused degraded service; we've rate-limited oversized requests and are following up." Ivan to join.

ivan (customer-ops): Acme responded: they accidentally forwarded internal test harness requests. They will stop the test and confirm. Asked for ETA on full restore.

jamie (eng-runtime): temp mitigation complete. Next step: patch runtime to clamp extremely large `max_tokens` at decode entrance (defensive code) + add metric and alert for token-spike vector. I'll open a PR.

ops-bot: Pager update: urgent -> resolved? status=mitigated by edge rule.

sasha (sre-oncall): rolling restart scheduled for 10 nodes that hit fragmentation. Doing drain + reprovision to clear fragmented CUDA heaps. ETA 12m.

telemetry-bot: Post-mitigation: error-rate down ~92%, OOM events dropped to baseline. Memory fragmentation still high on 3 nodes.

maria (oncall): escalation notes for postmortem: root cause = client-supplied `max_tokens` > runtime limits + missing defensive clamp at routing layer. Contributing factors: KV cache growth not bounded by session and insufficient alerting on token-skew.

jamie (eng-runtime): PR #4587 opened: `runtime: clamp max_tokens at 4096 and emit telemetry.token_overcap` — review requested. Will include unit tests and a canary rollout plan.

lee (support): Customer update sent: apologies + summary + ask to implement client-side cap. Acme confirmed they will patch their harness.

ivan (customer-ops): Acme provided logs and confirmed stop at 10:10Z. No further customer impact reported.

sasha (sre-oncall): all clear from oncall perspective after restarts and edge rule. Will file incident and assign postmortem owner.

maria (oncall): assigning postmortem to @jamie (eng-runtime). Please include timeline, detection gap, action items (edge validation, token alerts, KB for support).

jamie (eng-runtime): ack. Drafting postmortem and follow-ups.

ops-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Tags: gpu-oom, decode, max_tokens, customer-impact, edge-hotpatch.
